changes.headline: The reopen gave back a dollar; the freight correction reached the Gulf leg and the diesel crack printed below $100 again
changes.dek: Reopen: Brent near $115.7 and WTI near $102.3 in Monday morning reports (was $116.72 / $103.27 at Friday's settles). Baltic Week 43 is published (correcting Sunday's edition): TD9 WS 666 (was WS 830 in Week 42), TD3C WS 1208.13, TD22 $58.22 million. Diesel crack $97.49 on the latest validated print (Friday close $97.78), below $100 for a second print.. Sunday's reopen opened lower and stayed lower into Monday morning: Brent was quoted at $115.60 and WTI at $102.30 on Sunday evening after an early dip of $2.26 in Brent was partly recovered, and Monday morning reports still had Brent near $115.72. The weekend produced claims on the Rabigh refinery and the East-West Pipeline with two confirmed interceptions and no reported damage or flow interruption, and the first trade of the week paid about a dollar less for the story than Friday's close. The Baltic Exchange Week 43 weekly is published (week ending Oct 23, Baltic direct): TD3C WS 1208.13 with TCE $1,287,851 per day, TD22 at $58.22 million with TCE $451,905 per day, and TD9 at WS 666 with TCE under $210,400 per day, a second straight sharp dirty correction that has reached the Caribbean to Gulf leg. The diesel crack printed at $97.49 on the validated history refreshed this edition, below $100 for a second print after Friday's $97.78 close ended the sustained run that began Aug 17; the 3-2-1 crack is $52.07.
changes.balance_read: Claims without a confirmed outage are no longer adding premium at the reopen, while the two internals that tax Canadian heavy both eased at the margin: dirty freight corrected into the Gulf leg and the distillate crack's regime break has follow-through. Friday's Canadian tape still stands: synthetic returning on a traded print, December WCS wider on volume into November apportionment.
changes.publishers: OilPrice, Oct 25, 2026; Multiple, Oct 26, 2026; Reuters, Oct 23 to 24, 2026; Baltic Exchange Tanker Report Week 43 (week ending Oct 23, 2026); validated crack history refreshed Oct 26, 2026

changes.headline: Saturday's Saudi target list in full: Rabigh and the East-West Pipeline claimed, interceptions confirmed, Dhahran fire confirmed for Friday
changes.dek: New detail versus Sunday's edition: the full Reuters Oct 24 target list names the Rabigh refinery, East-West Pipeline pumping stations and a Yanbu facility; the coalition destroyed two missiles toward Yanbu and Taif; debris fell in Rabigh among other places. The Saudi Energy Ministry confirmed a Friday attack on a Dhahran administrative building caused a limited fire, no casualties.. The Houthis claimed on Saturday attacks on the Rabigh refinery, crude pumping stations and the East-West Pipeline, a facility at Yanbu, airports at Riyadh, Dammam and Najran, and the air base at Khamis Mushait (Reuters, Oct 24). The Saudi side confirmed destroying two ballistic missiles toward Yanbu and Taif and reported interception debris in Jeddah, Taif and Rabigh; whether the Rabigh debris relates to the refinery claim is unclear, Saudi Arabia has not commented on the claims, and no hit, damage assessment or flow interruption has been reported. The East-West Pipeline is the Kingdom's bypass to the Red Sea, so a confirmed hit there would be a different class of event; none is confirmed. Separately, the Energy Ministry confirmed a Friday attack on an administrative building at a Dhahran complex caused a limited fire with no casualties. The Revolutionary Guards' vessel claims are on day five to six with no advisory since Oct 22, no named vessel and no corroboration.
changes.balance_read: The claimed target set has climbed to first-class infrastructure while the confirmed column still reads interceptions, debris and one limited fire at an administrative building. Confirmed barrel impact of the campaign remains zero; the risk is concentrated in a single confirmation, not in the claim count.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Oct 24, 2026; Saudi Energy Ministry statement carried in the same coverage; UKMTO position unchanged since Update 088, Oct 22

changes.headline: Ukraine claimed Tuapse, Ryazan and Syzran overnight; the confirmed refinery-strike pause is over a week; the Lake Charles venue moves to Wednesday
changes.dek: Fresh unverified claims (Oct 25 to 26) on three refineries sit against a confirmed ledger whose Saturday strikes were petrochemical and missile supply targets. Calendar correction: the Louisiana refiner's third quarter call is Wednesday Oct 28 (company schedule, Sep 16), not Oct 30.. Ukraine claimed overnight strikes on the Tuapse refinery and on Ryazan and Syzran (RBC-Ukraine via wire live coverage, Oct 25 to 26), unverified with no damage assessment. Saturday's confirmed Ukrainian strikes were on Tolyattikauchuk, Omsky Kauchuk and an Ozon hub at Omsk, the Proton plant at Oryol and an aircraft at Yeysk, petrochemical and missile supply targets, and no refinery strike has been confirmed in over a week (last: Ryazan, Oct 16); the claim of Ryazan and Novoshakhtinsk strikes overnight Oct 23 to 24 remains uncorroborated, and Ryazan's main primary unit has been halted since Oct 15. DOE pages are unchanged: no award for either exchange round, posted contracts at 133.56 Mbbl to 13 companies, and the emergency exchange's cause still unstated. The refiner receiving that exchange reports Wednesday Oct 28, the first on the record venue for the cause question.
changes.balance_read: Refinery claims are arriving faster than confirmations; the Russian product subtraction resumes only if a damage assessment lands. The government balance sheet remains the tightest measured part of the system: 133.56 Mbbl lent, two awards unpublished, one emergency exchange unexplained.
changes.publishers: RBC-Ukraine via Guardian live coverage, Oct 25 to 26, 2026; Ukraine General Staff, Oct 24; SFG Media, Oct 24; DOE pages checked directly Oct 26, 2026; company schedule via Business Wire, Sep 16, 2026

flags.title: Hormuz flows above pre-war on exports; the vessel claims are silent for a fifth to sixth day; Saturday's claims named Rabigh and the East-West Pipeline
flags.detail: Kpler puts Middle East crude exports at 17.3 Mb/d in October, above the 16.9 pre-war average, with Hormuz flows at 11.7 Mb/d, about 82 percent of pre-war (Oct 22). The Revolutionary Guards' claims (seven vessels, then two supertankers on mines) have no named vessel and no independent corroboration after five to six days, no maritime advisory has issued since Oct 22, and US Central Command called the mine claims incorrect. On Saturday the Houthis claimed the Rabigh refinery, the East-West Pipeline and a Yanbu facility; the confirmed Saudi events were two interceptions toward Yanbu and Taif, debris in Jeddah, Taif and Rabigh, and a ministry confirmed limited fire at a Dhahran administrative building on Friday. Confirmed barrel impact remains zero. Trade the flow prints and confirmed incidents, not the claims. Trigger: Independent corroboration of any claimed incident, a named vessel, a flow print stepping down, or a Saudi statement of facility damage or a pipeline flow interruption

flags.title: Sanctions waiver: first US cargo at sea; no official deal per Bratislava; November tranche is the supply test
flags.detail: The first tanker under the waiver loaded 40,000 tonnes of diesel at Primorsk on Oct 22 and is heading for New York, arrival estimated Nov 7 (Reuters, shipping data). No signed supply contracts have been confirmed and no further loading has been reported. Slovakia's prime minister said after meeting Putin on Oct 23 that there is no official deal on Russian diesel exports to the United States and no exports yet (Reuters). The announced programme runs 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes thereafter. The binding constraint is Russian refining capacity: the Ryazan primary unit is halted since Oct 15, the plant was claimed struck again overnight Oct 23 to 24, and the largest refiner is stretching repairs from days into months. The import licence runs to Apr 7, 2027 and the waiver has no fixed expiry. Trigger: A first loading for the November tranche, a named US buyer or signed-contract confirmation, a Ryazan restart report, or a move in Congress to block the arrangement

flags.title: November apportionment 19 percent lights; December call unregistered; the synthetic verdict is scored
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment is Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, Oct 20). December's nowcast opens at persistence on those levels and no December judgment call is registered yet. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST, and on the published pattern (October's notice Sep 16, November's Oct 20) the December notice is expected around Nov 19 to 20, after nominations close, so the call must be registered as a judgment call rather than read off the notice. WCS Dec26 settled at -$28.50 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 23) on 555 lots, widening on traded volume, and the synthetic return verdict scored the same day at +$5.70 on 300 lots, below both registered lines. Trigger: Registration of a December judgment call before Nov 17, third-quarter volumes on Oct 30 and Nov 3 grading the synthetic tape verdict, or a second traded front-month move on Monday's settlement file

flags.title: Freight correction confirmed in Week 43 and reached the Gulf leg; clean tankers set records; the TD3C benchmark is on trial from today
flags.detail: Baltic Week 43 (week ending Oct 23): TD3C WS 1208.13 (TCE $1,287,851 per day), TD22 $58.22 million (TCE $451,905 per day), TD9 WS 666 (TCE under $210,400 per day), TD28 $14.26 million, a second straight sharp dirty correction on levels, with TD9's fall from WS 830 confirming the correction has reached the Caribbean to Gulf leg that prices competing heavy. Clean tankers diverged: product carrier earnings set records in the same week, with LR2 routes above $300,000 per day. A London trial over whether the TD3C benchmark should have been suspended during the war opens Oct 26. Levels remain multiples of pre-war; the easing trims the FOB discount pressure on WCS Houston at the margin, it does not shelter anything. Trigger: A Week 44 weekly stabilizing or re-accelerating, a fresh fixture at a new high or low, or a ruling/suspension in the benchmark trial

forward_calendar.what: Saudi energy minister Bahrain keynote; heating oil reserve bids due; private inventory survey
forward_calendar.detail: The minister keynotes on energy security and transitions at 09:50 AST in Bahrain, a headline venue into OPEC+ week on the published agenda, not a policy slot. Bids close on the Oct 21 Northeast heating oil reserve exchange (up to 315,000 barrels), deliveries to complete by Nov 13. The private survey for the week ending Oct 23 lands Tuesday afternoon, ahead of Wednesday's EIA report.

forward_calendar.what: EIA weekly report; Louisiana refiner third quarter call
forward_calendar.detail: The EIA reports the week ending Oct 23 at 10:30 a.m. ET. The refiner that received the Oct 23 emergency reserve exchange reports the same day (company schedule, Sep 16): the first on the record venue where the exchange's undisclosed cause can be asked.

Bids close on the Oct 21 Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve exchange (up to 315,000 barrels, the first use of the reserve since Hurricane Sandy in 2012), with deliveries to complete by Nov 13. Bid uptake is a dated measure of how tight the Northeast distillate balance remains into winter, four days after the diesel crack closed below $100.

forward_calendar.what: Imperial Oil and Cenovus Q3 results
forward_calendar.detail: The first of the Canadian majors to report the quarter that contains the fall turnaround windows. Upstream volumes are the first public test of whether Syncrude, Horizon and the Suncor plants returned on their guided schedules; no completion notices have been published for any of them. The synthetic return verdict, now scored on the tape at +$5.70, is graded against these volumes.

forward_calendar.what: OPEC+ meeting (Nov 1 to 2, most likely Nov 2)
forward_calendar.detail: Five analysts surveyed by Reuters (Oct 23) expect another modest December increase; delegates said after the Oct 5 meeting that the November increase was the last before a first-quarter pause. The spread between those two is the meeting's actual risk, carried into the highest settles of the episode.
Suncor operates Syncrude and the Base Plant and Edmonton refinery windows that ended in mid-October; its Q3 volumes are the closest public read on those returns ahead of September AER data.
Vermilion reports the quarter on Nov 4 (announced Oct 21). A smaller read on the basin than the majors, carried for calendar completeness.
MEG reports Q3 on Nov 5 (earnings call Nov 6), confirmed from the company's events calendar on Oct 24. A thermal producer read on the quarter.
Deliveries under the Oct 21 Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve exchange (up to 315,000 barrels) are to complete by this date.

December's Mainline nowcast opens at naive persistence on November's print (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert). No December judgment call is registered yet. Nominations close at 0700 MST.
